pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: NARRATIVE COMPOSITION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How do we develop a good narrative?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify elements of a narrative composition for comprehension
2. write texts based on the theme using good handwriting for effective communication
3. appreciate creativity and good handwriting in effective communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition

Teach
• Focus skill: identify elements of a narrative composition for comprehension.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we develop a good narrative?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
